title: Design an AI-Assisted Bulk Edit Review Flow
description: Design a customer-operations review flow where AI suggests lifecycle-stage edits, people verify account evidence, and only an approved version can produce mixed per-record outcomes.

seo.title: AI-Assisted Bulk Edit Review Flow System Design
seo.description: Design an AI-assisted bulk edit review with evidence checks, explicit approval, mixed record outcomes, cancellation, audit, and rollback.

premiumPreview.summary: Practice designing a tool that suggests lifecycle-stage changes for customer accounts, lets an operations specialist check the evidence, and applies only the records they approve.
learningOutcomes: Keep an AI suggestion separate from the edits a person has reviewed and approved.
Use current activity, invoice, and permission information to decide whether each edit is available.
Show successful, failed, and conflicted records separately after a bulk action.
Explain why Cancel does not mean the work was undone and when a separate rollback is safe.
premiumPreview.unlockDescription: Premium unlocks the complete account-review example, data and API contracts, mixed-result recovery, audit history, and the difference between Cancel and rollback.

editorial.searchIntent: Prepare a frontend system design answer for an AI-assisted bulk edit review flow.
editorial.readerPromise: The reader can explain how customer-record suggestions, evidence, review, approval, execution, audit, cancellation, and rollback remain separate.
editorial.uniqueAngle: Ground AI safety in a concrete customer-operations task: lifecycle-stage edits backed by last-activity and open-invoice evidence with truthful per-record recovery.

practice.candidatePrompt: Design a review flow for a customer-operations specialist using AI to propose lifecycle-stage changes across customer records. The user inspects last-activity and open-invoice evidence, removes records, and approves one proposal version before anything changes. Some records may succeed while others conflict, and Cancel may race with a late result. Explain how proposal, approval, execution, audit, and rollback stay separate so the interface never presents a suggestion or requested cancellation as confirmed product truth.
constraints: Eligibility uses current evidence and permission.
expectedDecisions: Separate generated content, trusted eligibility, local review, approval, and outcomes.
Bind one approval command to proposal, evidence, and record versions.
Reconcile mixed results, cancellation races, audit history, and compensating rollback.

mustCover: Separate generated suggestions, local review, approved commands, and actual outcomes.
Bind approval to reviewed proposal/evidence versions and current permission.
strongSignals: Separate successful and failed records, with recovery for each.
Cancel stays pending intent; rollback is a separate compensating command.
evaluationSpine.expertStretch: Permission churn, audit export, and reversible bulk undo.
evaluationSpine.redFlag: Proposal, optimistic result, or Cancel appears as confirmed product truth.
